events.credibility_reason: A version (v5, Sept 2025) was marked withdrawn before a v6 reappeared; reason unknown.

why: The statement was settled in 1994 (Dias da Silva–Hamidoune, journal of record), with further complete proofs by Alon–Nathanson–Ruzsa, Károlyi, Balister–Wheeler and Fehér–Nagy before the snapshot; Vu–Wood covers only a size range, so case. Nothing after the snapshot moves the question: Du–Pan proves a stronger abelian-group, k-fold theorem (variant, stronger form); Zhang (inverse problem), Terkel (Z_p^2), Ouyang (Lev's matching conjecture) and Goswami–Mistri (h-fold, large sets) are different questions. The close calls were Yang's preprint and the Lean file, both of which restate the full bound. Both are new proofs or formalisations of a theorem settled 30 years earlier. They resolve nothing, so I answered none rather than whole. Answering whole would credit a 2025/2026 resolution of a problem closed since 1994. For the Lean event, Aristotle only formalised a known argument, and that is none. ChatGPT is listed as an informal author, but the only quote says 'we followed the proof outline provided', and the outline is the 1995/96 Combinatorial Nullstellensatz proof. Nothing in it shows ChatGPT produced mathematics in the result, so that is none too (F12).
doubts: Answering Yang and Du–Pan as none/variant rather than whole is a judgement that re-proofs of a long-settled statement are not movement. If the harness wants re-proofs scored whole, Du–Pan (journal-accepted) would tier resolved after the snapshot. Pre-1994 papers were read only through secondary sources, but those sources agree. The ChatGPT contribution to the Lean file is unexplained.
